post.summary: The MCP endpoint: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP
post.description: Requires store.operate, and each tool additionally requires the rights core names on the equivalent REST route — list_orders needs orders.read, mark_order_paid needs orders.write, update_variant_inventory needs inventory.write, and so on. A refusal for want of a right comes back as a JSON-RPC error with code -32600 naming the missing right; a static admin token holds every right and is never refused. Four things a client has to know. (1) The body is JSON-RPC 2.0 and the reply is NOT the {data}/{error} envelope every other route uses — an MCP client cannot be asked to unwrap a second envelope, so this route is a deliberate, standing exception. (2) A JSON-RPC error comes back with HTTP 200 and a top-level error member; the HTTP status describes the transport, not the call. (3) A request with no id is a notification: it is answered 202 with an empty body. (4) 401 and 403 still arrive as the engine's own error envelope, from the middleware, before the body is read.

200.description: The JSON-RPC response, whether the call succeeded or failed.

202.description: A notification: accepted, nothing to say back.

get.summary: Every mutating tool call an agent has made
get.description: Requires store.operate. Reads are not recorded — only tools that declare they change state, plus a mutating call refused for want of a right, which is recorded with outcome error. No filters: newest id first, with limit and offset.

id.description: An integer or a string. Omit it to send a notification, which is answered 202 with no body.

params.description: For tools/call: {name, arguments}. The other methods take none.

McpJsonRpcResponse.description: Exactly one of result and error is present. The shape of result depends on the method: tools/list returns {tools: [McpTool]}, tools/call returns {content: [...]} with an isError flag when the tool refused.

McpTool.description: One entry in the tools/list result.

inputSchema.description: A JSON Schema object describing the tool's arguments.

annotations.description: ToolAnnotations arrived in MCP revision 2025-03-26 while this server advertises 2024-11-05, so this member is a forward-compatible extension rather than part of the advertised revision: a newer client reads it natively, an older one ignores it.

readOnlyHint.description: False for a tool that changes state. A store running the module read-only withholds those tools entirely, so every tool it lists reports true.

arguments.description: The arguments the agent sent, verbatim.

detail.description: Present only when the outcome is error: what the tool said.

called_at.description: RFC 3339. Before this release it was Go's own default layout ("2026-09-09 12:00:00 +0000 UTC"), which no date parser accepts — a script reading this field needs updating.
